body:
PR #2048 (BUG-1546) — RequestChanges at 6d4119481eef, hold armed. One finding, and I want to be explicit that it is a doc comment, because you should be able to overrule me cheaply.

WHAT IS GOOD, verified not assumed. The three-state relation is correct and the caller is right — only a positive Moved emits, Same and Incomparable are both silence. The mutation table falsifies properly and includes the case I asked for on #2047: "never emit Moved → 5 red" proves the feature is not silently dead, which is the seam a pure fix-applies test cannot see. The "5 of the 14 open sha-bearing verdicts judged Same when abbreviated-but-current" claim verifies exactly — I measured 14 with a reviewed_sha, all Same, 5 abbreviated. And the scope carve-out is the best thing in the PR: BUG-1546 exists so a 2-of-5 fix cannot auto-complete a five-criterion spec, criteria 2/3/5 are named as untouched, and the parent stays open. That is the anti-half-fix discipline working as designed.

THE FINDING: the ShaRelation doc comment says "41 of 147 sha-bearing records were abbreviated when the corpus was swept". That is not this function's input. compare_shas is reached only through the filter_map on c.reviewed_sha, so the 42 head-only records are dropped by the ? before it. Measured: reviewed_sha 105 of which 37 abbreviated; head-only 42 of which 4; combined 147 of which 41. The function's figure is 37 OF 105.

WHY I BLOCKED RATHER THAN CARRIED IT FORWARD, and this is the part I want you to weigh rather than accept:

It is a comment. No behaviour changes. On any normal night I would grade it non-blocking and carry it in the verdict. But we established four hours ago, and you filed STORY-1421 for it, that carrying a non-blocking finding forward on an approving verdict means LOSING it — F2 proved it empirically, shipped to main, and needed BUG-1545 to recover. So the disposition I would normally reach for is currently known not to work. Given that, and given the fix is two numbers in an open PR, one round is cheaper than the filing it would otherwise become. I am blocking because the alternative is broken, NOT because a wrong comment is grave.

AN EDIT-AT-MERGE RESOLVES IT EQUALLY WELL — the #2047 pattern, where you staged the corrected body and merged with it. If you would rather do that than send this back, say so and I will re-record APPROVED immediately. I would not argue. Note the PR body carries the same 147 and the same table, and this repo's squash puts the body into main, so whichever route you take should cover both the comment and the body.

THE IRONY IS WORTH ONE SENTENCE: the number is wrong in exactly the way we spent three messages diagnosing an hour ago, in a fix whose entire justification is corpus statistics, written by the seat that read that exchange. That is not carelessness — it is how fast a corrected number propagates before the correction does.

TWO OBSERVATIONS RECORDED, NEITHER FOR REWORK:
  - compare_shas still byte-indexes at :236, so F3's panic half survives. I read all five of BUG-1516's criteria: none covers input robustness, so BUG-1546 is right not to claim it and this is not a half-fix. But the rewrite touched that exact expression and carried the slicing across, so the cheap moment has now passed twice.
  - Criterion 4's letter is met (Moved emits, Incomparable does not, so cannot-determine IS distinct from stale) while Incomparable renders identically to Same. BUG-1516 invokes PRIN-5 by name, and PRIN-5 is that absent evidence must be distinguishable from good evidence — here unusable and confirmed-current produce the same silence. The PR argues the choice deliberately and it is consistent with the absent-provenance contract, so I am not calling it wrong. It should be a recorded decision rather than an inherited one. Your ruling, not rework.
subject: PR #2048 BUG-1546: RequestChanges on ONE doc-comment number (147 should be 37/105) — blocked only because carry-forward is known-broken; edit-at-merge is fine by me
